title: Choose heartbeat producer: kopia native vs sidecar vs hybrid
description: Decide between modifying kopia upstream/fork to emit a native heartbeat (option A) and a PowerShell sidecar that polls the upstream server's /api/v1/sources (option B). Option B ships today with zero kopia changes; option A is the right long-term answer. Research what kopia's existing notification framework + uitask manager already expose so we don't reinvent.
acceptance_criteria: Decision documented in epic's notes. If A: a small kopia patch is identified (estimated effort, file paths) for the next signing/build cycle. If B: heartbeat line format finalized (timestamped, structured key=value), emission cadence (60s default), output destination (daily_kopia.log vs separate heartbeat.log) — with rationale for each pick. Either way, ALL three consumer beads can implement against the agreed format.
notes:
DECISION: Option B (PowerShell sidecar polling existing kopia API). Rationale + spec below.

WHY OPTION B
============
Option A (kopia upstream patch / fork patch) is the architecturally cleaner answer but adds a build-cycle dependency. Option C (hybrid) just defers the choice. B ships in a day, uses already-existing API endpoints, and the resulting on-disk format is trivial for any future native heartbeat to reproduce — so an A-style replacement is drop-in compatible.

KOPIA EXISTS ENOUGH ALREADY
===========================
The upstream server already tracks everything we need:
- /api/v1/control/status — quick alive/health endpoint, no auth required for some fields
- /api/v1/tasks-summary — count of running/completed uitasks
- /api/v1/sources — per-source last-snapshot/in-progress state
- internal/uitask/uitask.go — uitask.Manager + Controller already produce ProgressInfo per running task
No need to add server-side machinery.

PRODUCER SPEC
=============
- New script: scripts/kopia_heartbeat.ps1
- New task:   \Backup\KopiaHeartbeat (At system startup, S4U, RunLevel=Highest, RestartOnFailure 3x1min — symmetric with \Backup\KopiaServer)
- Cadence: 60s loop, while-true, sleep at the bottom
- Auth: reads KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD from the existing DPAPI vault via get_kopia_server_password.ps1 (same path KopiaServer's launcher uses); HTTP Basic with username 'kopia' against the upstream API; pinned cert fingerprint from D:\KopiaServer\fingerprint.sha256
- On API error: still emit a heartbeat line marked server=error with the failure tag, so consumers can distinguish 'stuck producer' from 'stuck server'

OUTPUT
======
Path: C:\dev\kopia\logs\heartbeat.log (separate from daily_kopia.log so the wrapper log stays readable as 'one entry per nightly')
Format: one line per tick, ASCII, structured key=value
  [heartbeat] <ISO-8601-with-tz> server=<running|error> tasks=<N> [task=<kind>:<src>,progress=<pct>,duration=<s>]*
Rotation: when file exceeds 5 MB, rename to heartbeat.log.old (same pattern daily_kopia_backup.cmd uses for daily_kopia.log)

ON-DISK ESTIMATE
================
75 chars/line × 1440 ticks/day = ~110 KB/day. Rotated weekly is 770 KB. Negligible.

CONSUMERS (separate beads)
==========================
- bcp.3 (wrapper in-band guard): tail heartbeat.log; if newest line >3min old during a run, kill kopia child + FATAL
- bcp.4 (out-of-band watchdog): same staleness check on a faster cadence than 08:00 daily
- bcp.5 (backup-monitor.exe): replace data.rs:521 mtime check with heartbeat-line-timestamp parse

UPSTREAM-PR OPPORTUNITY (NOT FILED HERE)
========================================
A native --heartbeat-interval flag for 'kopia server start' that emits the same structured line via kopia's existing log channel would obviate the sidecar. Low priority because B works. If we ever upstream it, the sidecar can be retired and this format documented as the on-disk contract.
REVISED DECISION: Option A (native kopia heartbeat in this fork) supersedes the earlier Option-B sidecar pick.

Why the change: I was treating 'avoid kopia source changes' as a hard constraint when it isn't — this fork already rebuilds and re-signs kopia.exe routinely (sign-all.ps1 covers it, build path is 'go install ./...' from go.mod root). The sidecar was solving a non-existent build-cycle problem, at the cost of: another scheduled task, another auth path duplicating the vault read, and an extra process polling its own machine over HTTP just to mirror data the server already has.

Native is simpler:
- New goroutine in internal/server/ ticks every --heartbeat-interval (default off; set to 60s from start_kopia_server.ps1)
- Reads s.taskmgr active tasks directly (no API roundtrip, no auth, no JSON parse)
- Writes structured key=value lines either to stderr or to --heartbeat-file
- Includes per-task progress when uitask.Controller has it (bytes uploaded / total, ETA derived from elapsed/progress)
- On any internal error, emits 'server=error msg=...' rather than dropping the tick — so a stuck/dying server is still visible

Output destination: --heartbeat-file=C:\dev\kopia\logs\heartbeat.log. Format unchanged from the earlier sidecar spec, so bcp.3/.4/.5 consumers don't care which producer wrote the line.

bcp.2's scope is now: kopia fork patch (~100-150 LOC: one new file in internal/server/, one new flag pair in command_server_start.go, wiring) + start_kopia_server.ps1 gains --heartbeat-interval=60s --heartbeat-file=... + sign-all.ps1 unchanged (kopia.exe is already a target).

UPSTREAM PR OPPORTUNITY: this is a small, useful, generic feature. Worth filing upstream-kopia after we've validated the format here.

title: Heartbeat-based stall detection for kopia backup monitoring
description: Establish a predictable heartbeat signal so all monitors (wrapper in-band stall guard, KopiaBackupHealthCheck watchdog, backup-monitor.exe STATUS CARDS) can detect a hung backup in minutes instead of hours. Today, a stalled 'kopia snapshot create' is invisible until the 08:00 watchdog runs the morning after — there is no live in-band liveness check. Discovered while debugging the 2026-05-04 03:00 wrapper failure during the kopia-7s7 cutover.
design:
DESIGN GOAL
===========
A predictable 'pulse' every ~60 seconds while a backup or repo-server
session is alive, written somewhere any monitor can poll. Stale pulse
(no entry within ~3 minutes) -> stall, alert + kill.

OBSERVATIONAL PROPERTY (single source of truth)
==============================================
Some file or endpoint exposes a timestamped line per heartbeat:
  [heartbeat] <iso-ts> server=running uptime=Xs active_sources=N (snapshotting <source>)*

Cadence: 60s when active, 60s when idle (so absence is always a problem).
Persistence: written to a file consumers can poll without auth (no API
roundtrip cost on every check).

PRODUCER OPTIONS (research before deciding)
==========================================
A. Kopia upstream feature — add --heartbeat-interval to kopia server.
   PRO: native, no extra process. CON: needs upstream PR or fork patch +
   re-build cycle.
B. Sidecar PS script — wrapper forks a heartbeat emitter that polls
   the upstream server's /api/v1/sources every 60s and appends a line
   to daily_kopia.log (or a sibling heartbeat.log).
   PRO: ships today, no kopia changes. CON: extra process to manage.
C. Server log redirection — \Backup\KopiaServer's stdout already prints
   notifications etc; add a --log-heartbeat or use existing
   structured-log channel if one exists.

Option (B) is the cheapest path that delivers value immediately.
Option (A) is the right long-term answer.

CONSUMERS
=========
1. WRAPPER IN-BAND GUARD: while a kopia snapshot create is running, the
   wrapper checks heartbeat-line freshness every ~60s. If older than
   3min, kill the kopia child + FATAL. This is the regression-recovery
   path replacing the 120s repo-check timeout I dropped during 7s7.6.
2. OUT-OF-BAND WATCHDOG: extend check_backup_health.ps1 to flag
   heartbeat-stale even mid-run (currently it only checks at 08:00 for
   missing 'complete' line). Toast under KopiaBackup.HealthCheck.
3. backup-monitor.exe: STATUS CARDS gain a 'last heartbeat: Ns ago'
   line; turns red if > 3min. Live signal during in-flight runs.

LINKED ISSUES
=============
- kopia-7s7.6 (current wrapper rewrite) regressed the 120s repo-check
  timeout. The wrapper-side guard here SUPERSEDES that timeout once
  shipped, so the regression is acceptable as a temporary state until
  this epic lands.

title: Headless kopia server with vault-managed creds; KopiaUI and wrapper as REST clients
description:
Eliminate the race between KopiaUI's bundled kopia server and the daily backup wrapper's CLI invocations by collapsing to a single long-running kopia.exe server process that owns the repository. KopiaUI and daily_kopia_backup.cmd both become REST clients of that server.

Race observed Mon 05/04 03:00: wrapper preflight `kopia repository status` exited rc=1 in 0.43s with no stderr captured, while KopiaUI's bundled server (restored to working state Sun evening) was simultaneously holding the repo. No new Kopia snapshot was taken last night (wbadmin succeeded). This was the first nightly run with both processes healthy — race is structural, not transient.
design:
ARCHITECTURE
============
Three processes, only one holds the repo:

1. UPSTREAM: dedicated `kopia.exe server start` started by Scheduled Task at boot.
   - Stable port: 127.0.0.1:51515
   - Stable TLS cert/key (so fingerprint is invariant across server restarts)
   - --server-password from new DPAPI vault file (mirrors existing .kopia-pw.dat)
   - --config-file points at D:\KopiaRepo via filesystem connector
   - Owns the repo. Only process that opens it on disk.
   - Runs kopia's policy-driven maintenance internally.

2. KOPIAUI BUNDLED CHILD: spawned by KopiaUI as today (KopiaUI source at app/public/server.js:33-62 hardcodes `--random-password --address=127.0.0.1:0`; we are not modifying the Electron app).
   - Configured via repository.config of API/server type → bundled child runs as a proxy/client of process 1.
   - Does not open the repo on disk; race is gone by construction.

3. BACKUP WRAPPER: daily_kopia_backup.cmd issues `kopia --address=https://127.0.0.1:51515 --server-cert-fingerprint=<sha> snapshot create C:\dev` calls. Reads server password from the same vault helper.

VAULT PATTERN
=============
Mirror the existing scripts/.kopia-pw.dat layout:
- New file: scripts/.kopia-server-pw.dat (DPAPI LocalMachine, restrictive ACLs)
- New helper: scripts/get_kopia_server_password.ps1 (mirror of get_kopia_password.ps1)
- Already covered by existing .gitignore + .git/info/exclude defensive patterns
- SECRETS.md updated with a second recreate procedure

KOPIA CLI FLAGS (verified in this fork's source)
================================================
- cli/command_server.go:34 — `--server-password` with KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD env fallback
- cli/command_server_start.go:112-113 — `--tls-cert-file`, `--tls-key-file` for stable cert
- `--address=127.0.0.1:51515` — stable bind

OPEN QUESTIONS (answered before tasks land)
===========================================
- Q: Does KopiaUI in API mode still spawn its bundled child? A: YES (server.js:33-62 unconditional spawn). Acceptable — it's a stateless proxy, not a repo holder.
- Q: Does `kopia snapshot create` still emit the structured `snapshot summary source=...` line when invoked against a remote server? A: TBD before wrapper-via-api task lands; verify by spot-test against a temporary server during that task.

OUT OF SCOPE
============
- Modifying KopiaUI's source (Electron app) to use stable creds for its bundled child. The bundled child remains random-credential and stays a UI-only proxy.
- Migrating to Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp Vault. DPAPI LocalMachine + restrictive ACLs is the right vault scope for a single-host setup.

ROLLOUT
=======
Sequence: vault → cert → server task → KopiaUI reconnect → wrapper rewrite → preflight cleanup → docs.
Cutover risk: one nightly. Have wbadmin coverage as fallback during the wrapper switchover.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: personal/automation: post-run check + toast for wbadmin backup status
description:
Mirror of kopia-2ew but for Windows Server Backup (wbadmin). Currently we have no notification when wbadmin's nightly system-image backup fails or goes stale.

Sibling to kopia-2ew with no blocker dependency — they're independent backup surfaces.

Files (on personal/automation branch):
- New scripts/check_wbadmin_health.ps1: calls 'wbadmin get versions' + 'wbadmin get status', asserts newest backup is <24h old and last run succeeded. Posts toast via Show-Toast (extract or duplicate from check_backup_health.ps1 / post_summary_toast.ps1). Writes/clears WBADMIN_HEALTH_FAIL.flag.
- New scripts/create_wbadmin_health_check_task.ps1: registers daily scheduled task ~30min after wbadmin's window (interactive logon so toast reaches user session).
- Optional: register a separate AppId WBadminBackup.HealthCheck for visual distinction from kopia toasts (or reuse KopiaBackup.HealthCheck).

Tradeoff: clock-based, not event-driven. Real-time event-log subscription via wevtutil would catch failures the moment they happen, but ~3x the code for a rare benefit (failures discovered in-session vs. at 9am next day).

Why P2 not P1: kopia is the primary backup surface; wbadmin is the system-image safety net. Lose kopia notifications and you may miss real data loss; lose wbadmin notifications and you may miss bare-metal recovery prep going stale. The latter is recoverable on discovery.
notes: Implemented on personal/automation. Smoke-tested on this host: wbadmin checker PASS exit=0 (existing recent wbadmin backup detected). Includes em-dash regex fix in post_summary_toast.ps1 caught while smoke-testing.

DefaultOptions sets NumListBlobsWorkers: 3, so every provider validation run silently schedules 3 goroutines that do nothing. The concurrency test is designed to find races under concurrent list operations, but this entire category is bypassed. Fix: either implement the ListBlobs concurrency test, or set NumListBlobsWorkers: 0 in DefaultOptions with an explanatory comment.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Migrate pierrec/lz4 v2+incompatible to v4
description: In repo/compression/compressor_lz4.go:7, pierrec/lz4 v2.6.1+incompatible is used. The +incompatible tag means pre-Go-modules import. v4 has been canonical since 2020 with performance improvements and bug fixes. The compressor is registered as deprecated (decompression only for existing data), making migration low-risk. Fix: migrate to github.com/pierrec/lz4/v4, remove v2 from go.mod.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Replace golang.org/x/exp/constraints with stdlib cmp package
description: In internal/metrics/metrics_distribution.go:9, internal/units/units.go:10, and cli/show_utils.go:15, golang.org/x/exp/constraints is used for Integer/Float type constraints. The x/exp module is pinned to a May 2023 snapshot. Since Go 1.21 (and the project targets Go 1.25), these are available in stdlib via the cmp package. These three files are the only reason x/exp remains a direct dependency. Fix: replace with cmp.Ordered or inline constraint interfaces, drop x/exp from go.mod.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Migrate JWT v4 to v5 — v5 already present as indirect dependency
description: In internal/server/server.go:18, the codebase directly imports github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 (v4.5.2) while v5 (v5.3.0) is already pulled in as an indirect dependency. JWT v5 added security hardening around key validation and parser options. The API is nearly identical — jwt.ParseWithClaims and jwt.NewWithClaims signatures are unchanged. Fix: migrate to v5, remove v4 from go.mod.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: expireUnused stat-scans entire cache directory on every index refresh
description: In repo/content/committed_content_index_disk_cache.go:123-175, expireUnused reads the entire index cache directory and builds a map[blob.ID]os.FileInfo on every call to use() — which fires every index refresh (every 15 min or on flush). For long-lived repos with many .sndx files this adds latency to the refresh path while holding indexesLock exclusively. Fix: store only ModTime (not full os.FileInfo) in the map, and optionally maintain a persistent in-memory set.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Missing fsync before rename in disk index cache writeTempFileAtomic
description: In repo/content/committed_content_index_disk_cache.go:98-121, writeTempFileAtomic does not call f.Sync() before closing. Unlike filesystem_storage.go:createTempFileWithData (line 249) which does call f.Sync(), this path can lose data on crash — the renamed file may contain corrupt/zero data. Fix: add tf.Sync() before tf.Close(), matching the pattern in filesystem_storage.go.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: comparePrefix allocates string per entry during index iterations
description: In repo/content/index/id.go:146-161, comparePrefix's default case calls i.String() (which allocates via hex.EncodeToString) and strings.Compare on every non-empty prefix comparison. This is called per-entry during indexV1/V2.Iterate and IDRange.Contains. The code has a comment acknowledging it as 'slow path'. Fix: add a case for len(p)==1 comparing i.prefix directly, and for longer prefixes compare against raw bytes without string construction.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Object reader allocates fresh large byte slice per chunk
description: In repo/object/object_reader.go:106-125, openCurrentChunk allocates a fresh []byte of the chunk's full size (typically 4-8 MiB) every time the reader advances to a new chunk. The prior allocation becomes immediately GC-eligible. The gather package already provides pooled buffers but objectReader doesn't use them. Fix: store the chunk buffer in objectReader and reuse across chunk advances using gather.WriteBuffer pattern.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Index shard() calls k.String() per entry allocating O(N) strings
description: In repo/content/index/index_builder.go:157 and one_use_index_builder.go:71, shard() calls k.String() on every ID in the map to hash it for shard assignment. ID.String() calls hex.EncodeToString allocating a new string per call. For an index with millions of entries during epoch compaction, this is millions of heap allocations. The ID struct has raw bytes available via Hash(). Fix: replace io.WriteString(h, k.String()) with h.Write([]byte{k.prefix}) plus h.Write(k.Hash()).
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: contentCacheKeyForInfo allocates via fmt.Sprintf on every content read
description: In repo/content/content_manager_lock_free.go:106, contentCacheKeyForInfo uses fmt.Sprintf with %v on content.ID (which calls hex.EncodeToString) for every content read cache lookup. For restores of millions of files, this generates substantial GC pressure. For the common case where CompressionHeaderID/FormatVersion/EncryptionKeyID are all zero, the key is just the content ID. Fix: use bi.ContentID.Append(nil) to build the key and only append format discriminators when non-zero.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Cache sweepLocked performs I/O while holding listCacheMutex
description: In internal/cache/persistent_lru_cache.go:291-327, sweepLocked calls c.cacheStorage.DeleteBlob() (filesystem I/O) while holding listCacheMutex. This serializes all cache access during sweeps. The Put function already releases the lock around PutBlob I/O (lines 179/198), but sweepLocked (called just before) doesn't follow this pattern. During high-throughput backup/restore with a near-full cache, this creates a global serialization point. Fix: collect items to delete while holding lock, release lock, perform I/O, re-acquire to update heap.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: IterateContents defer drops parallel worker errors on early return
description: In repo/content/content_manager_iterate.go:115-116, when IterateContents returns early (e.g., maybeRefreshIndexes fails at line 147), the 'defer cleanup()' runs and drains the worker channel but its return value (the last worker error) is suppressed by //nolint:errcheck. The final 'return cleanup()' at line 155 does correctly return worker errors on normal completion, but early-return paths silently discard concurrent worker errors. Fix: use a named return and capture cleanup error in the defer.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: PersistentCache.Put double-panics on invariant violation
description: In internal/cache/persistent_lru_cache.go:170-207, the Put function uses a defer Unlock() registered while the mutex is held, then manually unlocks at line 179 for I/O. Between the manual unlock (179) and re-lock (198), a Panicf at line 187 fires if the protection overhead invariant fails. The defer will then try to unlock an already-unlocked mutex, causing a second panic (sync: unlock of unlocked mutex) that terminates the process with a confusing stack trace. Fix: re-lock before panicking, or restructure to avoid the dangling defer.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: IterateContents silently drops callback errors for uncommitted content
description: In repo/content/content_manager_iterate.go:144, the loop invoking the user callback for uncommitted content items silently discards all errors with '_ = invokeCallback(bi)'. For committed content (line 151), callback errors ARE propagated. This means early termination and error signaling do not work for uncommitted content. Callers like repo/manifest/committed_manifest_manager.go return errors from callbacks to signal failures. Fix: propagate the error with 'if err := invokeCallback(bi); err != nil { return err }'.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: RClone EmbeddedConfig missing kopia:sensitive struct tag
description: In repo/blob/rclone/rclone_options.go:18, the EmbeddedConfig field stores full rclone configuration (typically containing cloud storage credentials) as a plain string without the kopia:"sensitive" struct tag. All other credential fields across blob providers use this tag. ScrubSensitiveData will print this in plaintext via 'kopia repository status'. Fix: add kopia:"sensitive" struct tag.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Content-Disposition header injection via unsanitized fname parameter
description: In internal/server/api_object_get.go:41, the fname query parameter is directly interpolated into the Content-Disposition header without sanitization. A double-quote in the value terminates the filename parameter, allowing parameter injection. Go's net/http mitigates CRLF injection since Go 1.5, but quote-based attacks remain. Fix: use mime.FormatMediaType("attachment", map[string]string{"filename": p}) for RFC 6266-compliant encoding.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Prometheus /metrics endpoint requires no authentication
description: In cli/command_server_start.go:260-322, the /metrics endpoint is registered directly on the mux router with no authentication. It exposes runtime metrics (goroutine counts, memory stats, HTTP request counters) to any network-reachable client. All other endpoints require auth. Fix: wrap with srv.RequireServerControlAuth(promhttp.Handler()) or restrict to localhost.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Auth and session cookies missing HttpOnly and SameSite flags
description: In internal/server/server.go:235-240 and 825-829, both Kopia-Auth (JWT) and Kopia-Session-Cookie (CSRF session) cookies are set without HttpOnly or SameSite flags. The session cookie value is used to derive the CSRF token, so missing HttpOnly nullifies CSRF protection — JavaScript can read the cookie and compute the token. Fix: add HttpOnly: true and SameSite: http.SameSiteStrictMode to both cookies.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: SSH dial error leaks ClientConfig internals via format string
description: In repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go:525, when SSH dial fails, the error is formatted with %#v on the *ssh.ClientConfig struct. The Auth field contains ssh.AuthMethod closures that capture password strings. This internal structure will appear in logs and error messages. Fix: remove %#v of config from the error, log only the address.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Unbounded HTTP request body read enables memory exhaustion DoS
description: In internal/server/server.go:365, io.ReadAll(rc.req.Body) is called on every authenticated API request with no size limit. An authenticated attacker can send an arbitrarily large request body to exhaust server memory. The gRPC path is correctly bounded at 20MB (MaxGRPCMessageSize) but the HTTP path has no equivalent. Fix: wrap body with http.MaxBytesReader before reading.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: JWT algorithm not validated in auth cookie parsing
description: In internal/server/server.go:252, isAuthCookieValid passes a key func to jwt.ParseWithClaims that does not validate the signing algorithm. Any HMAC variant (HS384, HS512) will be accepted. Additionally, the issuer and audience fields set at cookie generation (lines 274-275) are never verified on parse. This is a known JWT vulnerability pattern (algorithm confusion). Fix: add algorithm type assertion and use jwt.WithIssuer/jwt.WithAudience parser options.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/comprehensive-review-fixes

title: Rename the product/stack from Kopia to RustBack
description:
Decision 2026-05-17: the rewritten stack will be branded RustBack (Rust Backup and Recovery on Windows), retiring the 'Kopia' name. The fork keeps the Kopia name only for the legacy/upstream code; all new-stack identity becomes RustBack.

Pre-OSS-release work — does NOT block sub-project 0 or the cutover; sub-project 0 keeps the current backup-* binary names. Sequence the rename after the legacy stack is retired (renaming mid-cutover would churn signing, scheduled-task XMLs, and the URL protocol while they're still load-bearing).

Scope to settle + execute when scheduled:
- Binary naming scheme: rustback-server / rustback-monitor / rustback-mirror / rustback-dump / rustback-indexer / rustback-tray / rustback-file / rustback-image  — OR keep backup-* as generic and brand only the product. Decide one scheme.
- Crate name (currently 'backup-monitor' in Cargo.toml) -> rustback. crates.io 'rustback' confirmed free 2026-05-17.
- URL protocol: kopiamonitor: -> rustback: (touches register_backup_monitor_toast.ps1, the toast launch URI in src/server/toast.rs APP_USER_MODEL_ID + LAUNCH_URI, the notification chain).
- Repo identity: decide whether the new stack moves to its own repo or stays in the kopia fork under a rustback/ tree.
- Filesystem paths: C:\BackupServer, C:\BackupMonitorIndex, D:\Recovery cache names, jobs.toml location.
- signing/sign-all.ps1 target list + D:\Recovery cache filenames.
- Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md, architecture-vision.md, CLAUDE.md, oss-dev/SETUP.md + SECURITY.md, the roadmap spec.
- Scheduled tasks: BackupServerWaker-* -> RustBackWaker-* (or chosen scheme).

Naming research backing the decision is in the 2026-05-17 conversation: 'rustback' crate free, no trademark/company collision; note the connotation caveat (rust-back is also a corrosion/rerusting term) was reviewed and accepted by the owner.

Acceptance: all new-stack binaries, crate, URL protocol, paths, scheduled tasks, signing config, and docs use the RustBack identity; no 'kopia'/'Kopia' references remain except where they correctly refer to the legacy/upstream code.
acceptance_criteria: All new-stack binaries, crate name, URL protocol, paths, scheduled tasks, signing config, and docs carry the RustBack identity; remaining 'Kopia' references only describe legacy/upstream code. Scheduled after legacy retirement.

title: [feature] DPAPI password resolution in jobs.toml (gated on Phase 2.x)
description:
Per decision #12 of this plan, `jobs.toml` should support DPAPI
references in the `env` map:

```toml
env = { KOPIA_PASSWORD = "@dpapi:scripts/.kopia-pw.dat" }
```

The string is dereferenced at worker-spawn time via native DPAPI
(windows-rs `CryptUnprotectData`, LocalMachine scope) and the
plaintext bytes flow into the child's env block.

**Fix**:

1. Add a small `@dpapi:<path>` parser in `src/server/worker.rs`'s env-
   prep step.
2. Use windows-rs `Windows::Win32::Security::Cryptography::
   CryptUnprotectData` to decrypt the file's contents.
3. Pass the resulting bytes (zeroed after use) into the child's env
   via `std::process::Command::env`.
4. Plaintext NEVER touches disk; NEVER logged; NEVER appears in
   `events.jsonl`.

**Gated on**: Phase 2.x worker rewrites. Today's PS scripts already
handle DPAPI via `get_kopia_password.ps1`; not needed until
backup-server invokes `kopia.exe` directly.

**Parent**: kopia-0dr. **P3**, gated.
**Plan**: keen-dancing-sparkle.md §"Bead records" #20.

title: rehash_dst_into_manifest runs silently — multi-TB torn-recovery pass emits no progress events
description: When mirror_file enters the torn-recovery branch with a large partial dst, the rehash_dst_into_manifest call (cbt.rs:340) runs before the ProgressReporter is created (cbt.rs:215). For a 2.46 TB partial dst that takes ~4.5 hours of sequential read at 150 MB/s, the progress JSONL file gets ZERO events during the entire rehash. Operators can't distinguish 'hung' from 'busy' for hours.\n\nObserved on 2026-05-15 14:01 validation run: WIB tree launched at 14:39:05 processing the d88fe253-…vhdx. After the first two small files completed quickly (5efa1bda, BackupSpecs.xml), the progress file went silent for 36+ minutes. Live I/O counter showed 150 MB/s reads ongoing — process was actively rehashing, but invisibly. Same gap would apply to first-run or any case where a multi-TB file enters mirror_file with a populated dst.
design:
Two complementary fixes:

1. Initialize ProgressReporter BEFORE the run-mode decision, with a 'phase' annotation (rehash | main). Emit a 'phase_start' event when entering rehash, periodic 'rehash_progress' events at progress_interval_sec, and 'phase_end' on completion. Same cadence as the main loop's chunk_progress.

2. Alternatively, accept that rehash is just a hot read pass and emit at least a one-line summary on entry/exit ('rehashing partial dst, bytes=X' / 'rehash complete, dst=X bytes, hashes_loaded=Y').

Option (1) is more uniform and useful but touches more code. Option (2) is one-liner-level work. Recommend (1) since the gap can be hours wide.

No behavior change — purely observability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) During torn-recovery rehash, progress events emit at progress_interval_sec cadence so operators can see live I/O progress. 2) Rehash events distinguishable from main-loop events (phase tag or distinct event name). 3) Existing tests still pass; rehash speed is not regressed by event emission overhead.
close_reason: fixed

title: daily_d_replica.ps1 alignment phase logs nothing on no-op — invisible execution makes verification hard
description: The Phase 2a alignment block added in kopia-8fc only logs when it takes an action (Remove-Item or Rename-Item). On the common steady-state path — dst dated folder name already matches src — the block silently no-ops. There's no log line confirming 'alignment checked, no action needed'.\n\nObserved on 2026-05-15 14:01 validation run: subtree list at 14:01:32.25 was immediately followed by 'Accounting launching' at 14:01:32.29, with zero output in between. The alignment did execute correctly (we verified empirically) but the log gives no positive confirmation. If alignment logic regresses to a bug where it silently fails to run, we wouldn't notice until a wbadmin rotation forced a re-mirror.
design: Add a single Write-Log line per WindowsImageBackup machine-dir inspected, e.g. '[WindowsImageBackup] alignment check under ChrisLaptop2: src=\"Backup 2026-05-15 090023\", dst=\"Backup 2026-05-15 090023\" (match)' for the no-op case. Existing action paths already log; just close the gap on the steady-state branch.\n\nKeep the log volume bounded — one line per machine-dir, not per file. Today that's 1 line per run.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On a steady-state run (dst matches src already), the log contains an alignment-check confirmation per machine-dir. 2) Existing rename / remove log lines unchanged. 3) Log volume increase is bounded (O(machineCount) per run, typically O(1)).
close_reason: fixed

title: kopia-rewrite: unified Rust backup for Windows (open-source target)
description:
Long-term vision: replace kopia (Go) with a native Rust backup system that unifies file-level deduplicated backup (kopia's strength) and block-level system imaging (Macrium Reflect's strength) on Windows, then open-source for community use.

Inspired by but not necessarily compatible with: kopia (file-level dedup, encryption, snapshot/restore, multi-backend), rustic/restic (Rust impl, dedup, restic-format), Macrium Reflect (block-level VHDX, bare-metal restore). Goal is to combine all three capability categories in one signed Rust binary stack on Windows first, then extend to Linux/macOS.

This is a multi-year vision, not an immediate work item. It exists as a guiding document so near-term architectural decisions (Backup Server design, worker boundary choices, lib vs binary splits) can be evaluated against it.

Strategy: Ship-of-Theseus. Build the Backup Server scaffolding first (kopia-bs sub-epic) with kopia.exe + wbadmin.exe as third-party workers. Progressively replace each worker with native Rust as the architecture proves out. Keep the current personal-stack production running throughout (the user explicitly committed 2026-05-14 to maintaining the kopia-based stack for local DR while the rewrite proceeds).

Open-source readiness gates: clearly-named identity (not kopia2), Apache-2.0 license, README/CONTRIBUTING/CODE_OF_CONDUCT, security disclosure process, public docs, reproducible builds, signed releases (Trusted Signing infrastructure already in place at C:\dev\kopia\signing\), semantic versioning, and a hard scope statement up front. Better to publish 'Windows-first, file+block backup, no cloud yet' early than wait for full kopia parity.

Highest-risk crypto/format areas: don't DIY encryption (use aes-gcm or chacha20poly1305 from RustCrypto), hashing (blake3 / sha2 from RustCrypto), content splitter (fastcdc crate). Repository format is a fork-in-the-road: kopia-compatible-on-disk (huge spec implementation) vs new format (migration tooling). Decide explicitly.

See: architecture-vision.md at C:\dev\kopia\architecture-vision.md for the full design + decision log + lessons-learned. This bd entry is the vision-level anchor; concrete work happens in child epics.
notes: Created 2026-05-14 during DR + architecture audit session. User context: 'My longterm vision is to rewrite kopia into our rust architecture (we are just figuring out how to clean up our architecture), so we have a single unified backup solution for Windows that covers all scenarios (similar to Macrium Reflect). I could then post this to github as an open source utility available for community contribution and testing.' Restic / rustic_core evaluation pending (research agent spawned). wbadmin alternatives research also pending.

title: [chore] DR hardening: cache pre-built kopia.exe (and helper binaries) offline-accessible for bare-metal recovery
description:
Today's bare-metal recovery from D:/E: requires building kopia.exe from source (Go toolchain + 'go install github.com/kopia/kopia') OR downloading from kopia.io. Both require internet. The backup-monitor binaries (backup-monitor.exe, backup-mirror.exe, backup-dump.exe, backup-indexer.exe) require 'cargo build --release' which means Rust toolchain + crates.io + 30+ min build time.

In a real outage scenario (especially one that takes out C: + internet, e.g., ISP issue plus drive failure), this turns a 1-hour recovery into a multi-hour blocker waiting for connectivity.

Action items:
1. Create D:\Recovery\ (or use an unused corner of D:) — outside replica EXCLUDE_TOP so it's mirrored to E:, OR explicit add to EXCLUDE if we want it D:-only.
2. Cache signed releases of:
   - kopia.exe (from a tagged kopia.io release — version-pin in a README)
   - backup-monitor.exe / backup-mirror.exe / backup-dump.exe / backup-indexer.exe (latest signed builds from C:\dev\backup-monitor\target\release\)
3. Add a one-page README at D:\Recovery\README.md with the recovery runbook (link to SECRETS.md procedure, list of git clone URLs for the source repos, the kopia repo path, etc.).
4. Refresh schedule: weekly or monthly hook into sign-all.ps1 to copy newly-signed binaries to D:\Recovery\ if their hash changes.
5. Bonus: dd the Win11 ISO at D:\Win11_25H2_English_x64_v2.iso to a USB stick stored offsite — D:'s GPT-NTFS is not directly bootable.

Out of scope for this issue:
- Bootable rescue medium (separate concern; the Win11 ISO is good enough)
- Off-machine cloud storage of binaries (overkill for personal scale)

Discovered during 2026-05-14 DR audit. Lower priority than the password verification issue because internet-recoverable, but worth doing as a 'recovery in < 30 min' target rather than 'recovery in < 3 hours'.
notes: Related to kopia-bmy (the replica cutover already proved E: openable-standalone with the kopia password). Indexer output (D:\BackupMonitorIndex) is intentionally NOT cached here because the index is regeneratable from snapshots via run_indexer_backfill.cmd — see feedback-index-must-stay-on-d.
close_reason: fixed

or PowerShell Studio non-interactive session). Confirmed during the
kopia-5ua rsync seed today: the run was a clean PASS but the
[toast] failed emission line shows in the log.

scheduled-task runs (InteractiveToken) work fine; manual/background
invocations don't.

2. Use the BurntToast PowerShell module (handles the WinRT loading

3. Switch to a small native .exe (or sigcheck-style) that posts a

Decide once - then apply to daily_d_replica.ps1, weekly_replica_verify.ps1,
and any future helper script. Cosmetic in production (toasts ARE
emitted by the InteractiveToken scheduled task runs) but pollutes
manual-invocation logs with red ERROR lines.

title: Fix empty-Message Write-Log crash in weekly_replica_verify.ps1 catch path
description:
weekly_replica_verify.ps1 crashes when its catch block tries to log an
exception with an empty Exception.Message. Symptom: kopia repository
connect succeeds, then Write-Log fails with 'Cannot bind argument to
parameter Message because it is an empty string', BACKUP_REPLICA_VERIFY_FAIL.flag
gets touched, sticky FAIL state in backup-monitor's Replica STATUS
CARD even though the underlying replica is fine.

Connect succeeds, log shows: '[connect] Connected to repository.' then
immediately '[result] ERROR: Cannot bind argument to parameter Message
because it is an empty string'.

Root cause: somewhere in the verify or catch path, Write-Log "" or
similar is called. Write-Log has [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Message
which PowerShell rejects empty strings for.

Fix: guard Write-Log calls in the catch handler against empty/null
$_.Exception.Message - fall back to ($_.ToString()) or a literal
'unknown error' string. Also audit any other Write-Log call sites
for the same issue.

   stderr padding doesn't trigger the mandatory-string rejection.

2. catch handler: derives a non-empty error message via fallback
   chain (Exception.Message -> $_.ToString() -> literal), so

title: wbengine.exe lingers idle, blocks wrapper preflight up to 60min
description:
Today's manual nightly (2026-05-07 06:06) hit 'WARNING: wbengine.exe still running, waiting up to 60 min' even though wbadmin had completed at 02:42. wbengine.exe (PID 136908 today) was idle (0ms CPU over 5s, 26MB working set) but resident — Windows leaves the service loaded after a backup completes. The wrapper's preflight (daily_kopia_backup.cmd lines 130-150) only checks tasklist for the PROCESS, not whether it's actively backing up.

Manually killed wbengine.exe to unblock; wrapper detected it gone within 60s and proceeded normally. Windows relaunches the service automatically on next wbadmin invocation, so killing was safe.

Possible fix: extend the preflight to check whether wbengine is actually doing work (e.g. via 'wbadmin get status' or by checking process CPU activity over a sampling window) before assuming it's a blocking backup in progress. Or shorten the 60-min wait if wbengine.exe has been idle for >N seconds.

Not currently happening to nightly runs (the 03:00 run hits wbengine while it's actively backing up, which is the intended behavior). Only an issue for ad-hoc/recovery runs after the morning wbadmin window.
notes: 2026-05-07: Fixed in same commit as kopia-i1p/kopia-dgd. Replaced the tasklist-based wbengine.exe presence check with `wbadmin get status` parsing. The previous check matched on process presence alone, but Windows leaves wbengine.exe loaded for a while after a backup completes — that residual idle process triggered the 60-min wait on ad-hoc/recovery runs. New check looks for "No backup or recovery operation is currently running." in wbadmin's stdout (also used inside the wait loop). Verified standalone: with no active backup, the check correctly identifies idle and skips the wait. Acceptance: next ad-hoc run after a completed wbadmin should log "[preflight] wbadmin idle" instead of "WARNING: wbengine.exe still running, waiting up to 60 min".

title: Separate kopia client cache directories to stop temp-file rename races
description:
Both KopiaUI's bundled kopia.exe server (in client/proxy mode) and the daily_kopia_backup.cmd's elevated kopia.exe client share the same cache directory at %LOCALAPPDATA%\kopia\e54bae130c7f6c69\server-contents\ (it's keyed by repo identity in repository.config and both processes use the same client config). They race on temp-file rename:

  unable to add kXXX to cache-storage: ... rename ...f.tmp.YYY ...f: Access is denied.

Hundreds of these per nightly. Kopia handles them as non-fatal (retries 2x then proceeds; 'ignored_errors' counter ticks for genuine source-file errors only — these cache-write errors don't even bump that). But they're noise that shouldn't be there architecturally — every cache miss is a wasted re-fetch from the server.

Two real fixes:
1. Pass --cache-directory=<unique-path> to the wrapper's kopia.exe invocations (cheapest)
2. Maintain a separate client config for the wrapper at e.g. %APPDATA%\kopia\wrapper.config with its own cacheDirectory; modify daily_kopia_backup.cmd's KOPIA_CFG to use it. Cleaner separation, also stays out of KopiaUI's way.

KopiaUI keeps its config at the standard path (per the cutover); the wrapper gets the second config.
acceptance_criteria: Daily nightly run produces zero 'unable to add kXXX to cache-storage' / 'Access is denied' lines in daily_kopia.log. Verified by grep -c on the next two consecutive nightlies. Cache directories visible: ls %LOCALAPPDATA%\kopia\ shows TWO client cache dirs (one per repo-identity hash), and lsof / handle.exe shows no overlap of file handles between the wrapper's kopia.exe and KopiaUI's bundled kopia.exe.
notes: Reopened 2026-05-06 — closure reason was wrong. The --cache-directory in KOPIA_CFG approach was rejected by kopia at runtime (only valid on 'repository connect', not on status/snapshot/etc). See commit 54c4e033 which backs out the broken approach. CORRECT FIX: option 2 from the original description — create a separate wrapper config via 'kopia repository connect --config-file=%APPDATA%\kopia\wrapper.config --cache-directory=%LOCALAPPDATA%\kopia-wrapper-cache ...' (one-time elevated setup with full repo connect args), then change KOPIA_CFG in the wrapper to point at wrapper.config. The cache-directory will be persisted IN that config file's caching: section. Original acceptance criteria still apply.

The cacheDirectory is now baked into the config's caching: section, where kopia respects it on every subsequent command. Setup script (scripts/connect_wrapper_config.ps1) is idempotent and DPAPI-decrypts the server password from .kopia-server-pw.dat. Tonight's nightly will exercise it; expected: zero 'Access is denied' temp-file rename warnings.

title: Stall-guard WRAPPER_PID resolution fails under S4U scheduled-task context
description:
2026-05-05 03:00 nightly logged 'WARNING: could not resolve wrapper PID; stall guard not started' — the heartbeat watchdog (bcp.3) didn't actually start for the first real S4U-context run.

The wrapper's PID-resolution snippet:
  for /f %%P in ('"%PS_BIN%" -NoProfile -Command "(Get-WmiObject Win32_Process -Filter \"ProcessId=$PID\").ParentProcessId"') do set WRAPPER_PID=%%P

Worked fine when tested from interactive cmd in this session, but produced empty output when invoked from the scheduled task running as user david via S4U. Possible causes: WMI access restrictions under S4U-elevated context, the nested-quoting escape getting mangled differently in scheduled-task cmd vs interactive, or PowerShell $PID not being set under -NoProfile -Command in some edge case.

Functional impact: zero last night (the run succeeded), but the stall guard is supposed to be the in-band fail-fast mechanism. If a real stall hits before this is fixed, the wrapper would hang until the 08:00 watchdog catches it.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) PID resolution works under S4U context — verified by a fresh nightly run logging '[stall-guard] launching watchdog (wrapper PID=NNNN)' instead of WARNING. Or (b) Switch to a different mechanism that doesn't depend on cmd-batch+nested-PS quoting (e.g., write the wrapper's PID via a tiny .ps1 helper invoked from the wrapper, or have the wrapper invoke heartbeat_watchdog.ps1 with an environment variable instead of a command-line arg). Verified by waiting for tomorrow's nightly + grepping the log for the [stall-guard] launching line.
notes: 2026-05-07: Re-investigated. Root cause was NOT S4U/DCOM as originally suspected — it is cmd's for/f parser mangling the quoted-path command. Reproduced interactively: for /f %P in ('"%PS_BIN%" args') returns empty AND prints "filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect". The PS 5.1 binary path with embedded backslashes and a quoted-path-followed-by-args trips cmd's parser; outer quotes get stripped wrong. Even today's manual 06:06 run logged the WARNING despite running the new ntdll-based script — because the script never ran from the wrapper's for/f. Fix: replaced for/f with temp-file pattern (redirect to %TEMP%/kopia_wrapper_pid.txt then set /p). Verified via standalone cmd test: WRAPPER_PID populates correctly. Same broken pattern existed at line 231 (check_backup_errors.ps1) — fixed in same commit, addresses kopia-dgd. Acceptance pending: tomorrow's 03:00 nightly should log [stall-guard] launching watchdog (wrapper PID=NNNN) instead of the WARNING.

title: Track B: benchmark kopia API search latency vs sidecar index
description: Spike: with the upstream \Backup\KopiaServer running, measure end-to-end latency for 'find files matching <substring> across 30 historical snapshots' via the kopia REST API vs the current .jsonl.gz/.names.idx sidecar approach. Decision gate: if API path is sub-500ms (or comparable to sidecar) for typical queries, drop the entire indexer and Track A. If significantly slower, proceed with Track A.
acceptance_criteria: Three workloads benchmarked: (1) exact basename match across all latest-1 snapshots, (2) substring across all snapshots backfilled, (3) glob across all snapshots backfilled. Each measured 5x via kopia /api/v1 endpoints AND via existing sidecar reads. Results table with median/p95 latencies and any error rates. Recommendation written into epic notes: pursue A, pursue B, or pursue both (A as immediate win + B as long-term replacement).
notes:
BENCHMARK COMPLETE. Decision: keep the sidecar — Track B fails.

Workloads tested (Cargo.toml / config.json substring across kopia snapshots; 64-67 snapshot OIDs in the live repo today):

WORKLOAD 1 (single snapshot)
  Sidecar (zcat .jsonl.gz | grep): 411-761ms hot
  API (kopia ls -r --json):         63-107ms
  -> API wins per-snapshot by ~6x

WORKLOAD 2 (cross-snapshot, .jsonl.gz / path mode)
  Sidecar: 8.6s cold, 299ms hot, up to 44s for the bigger Cargo.toml run that actually traversed 24MB compressed
  API:     ~5s, no caching layer to amortize
  -> Roughly comparable at scale

THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL — find_restore.rs has a TWO-TIER reader (src/pages/find_restore.rs:870-906):
  Tier 1 (filename mode, the common case): mmap .names.idx (binary basename index)
  Tier 2 (path mode, query contains / or \): zcat .jsonl.gz

The .names.idx total is 12.7 GB across 67 files (raw, not compressed) — cat /dev/null run cold=15.5s hot=3.3s. With basename match CPU on top, real filename-mode searches today run in seconds.

Kopia's REST API has NO equivalent for basename-mode fast scan. Replacing the sidecar with API means rebuilding the .names.idx fast path inside backup-monitor — at which point we still maintain a basename index, just in a different storage. No win.

CONCLUSION: Track B (defer to API) is not viable. The sidecar's value is the .names.idx basename index amortization, which the API cannot replicate without us reinventing it. Track A (delta-from-prior to reduce nightly indexer cost) is the correct path forward. The 0o3 epic stays scoped to making the existing sidecar cheaper, not deleting it.
close_reason: Benchmark complete. Track B fails — kopia API has no basename-mode equivalent, sidecar's .names.idx amortization is load-bearing. Proceed with Track A (delta-from-prior).

title: Incremental kopia snapshot indexing (delta-from-prior)
description: Today the nightly indexer skips already-indexed snapshots (snapshot-level incremental at the OID level). But each new nightly snapshot has a NEW root OID by construction, so it gets walked from scratch via 'kopia ls -r' — even though 99%+ of paths are identical to the prior nightly. For C:\Users\david at ~1M files, that's minutes of work nightly to re-emit unchanged paths. Build a delta-from-prior mode so per-night work scales with the actual change set (typically tens to hundreds of files), not the total file count. Backfill-mode benefits even more dramatically (n+1 walks instead of n×walk_cost).
design:
TWO TRACKS, RUN IN PARALLEL
===========================

TRACK A — Delta-from-prior (primary, lowest-risk shipping path)
----------------------------------------------------------------
For each new latest-1 snapshot per source, locate the prior latest-1's
existing index file (kopia-<prev-oid>.jsonl.gz / .names.idx). Run
'kopia diff <prev-oid> <new-oid>' to get added/removed/modified path
list. Build new index = read prior index + apply delta + write new
files.

PRO: same on-disk format. find_restore.rs and backup-monitor.exe
readers unchanged. Failure mode is "fall back to full walk" — never
worse than today.

CON: complexity around partial-state recovery (crash mid-write),
correctness invariants on apply-delta, edge cases like first
snapshot per source (no prior to delta from -> full walk).

TRACK B — Defer to kopia API (research/benchmark, may obviate Track A)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
With the upstream \Backup\KopiaServer running 24/7 (post-cutover
2026-05-04), every backup-monitor search could query kopia's existing
B-tree-backed indexes directly via /api/v1/sources/<src>/list or
similar endpoints, with no sidecar indexes at all.

PRO: zero index maintenance. backup-indexer.exe goes away.
D:\BackupMonitorIndex\ goes away. Always-fresh by definition.

CON: every search hits kopia API. Need to benchmark "type a
filename and see results across 30 historical snapshots" — if
latency exceeds ~500ms, UX regresses.

Track B is RESEARCH-FIRST. Decision point: if kopia API can serve
sub-500ms searches against 30 snapshots × 1M paths each, Track A is
unnecessary and we delete the indexer entirely.

TRACK C — Rolling composite index (NOT pursued — bigger surface)
----------------------------------------------------------------
One global (source, path) -> [(oid, size, mtime), ...] index with
huge dedup. Massive storage win and elegant data model, but requires
rewriting both find_restore.rs and backup-monitor's reader. Filed as
context only; revisit if Track B benchmark fails AND Track A is judged
too complex.

ROLLOUT
=======
1. Track B benchmark first (single-day spike).
2. If B is viable -> design B properly, kill A.
3. If B is not viable -> design A properly, ship.
close_reason: Epic complete. All children closed: kopia-0o3.1 (Track B benchmark — sidecar must stay) ✓; kopia-0o3.2 (Track A delta-from-prior) ✓; kopia-0o3.3 (architectural decision) ✓. Net result: nightly indexer cost dropped from minutes (full kopia ls -r walks) to seconds (delta apply against prior), with full-walk fallback on any failure. Sidecar format untouched, no reader changes. Production-validated 2026-05-07.

title: Speed up Find & Restore first-search (currently 30-45s with 199 MB wbadmin index)

UI thread is blocked the entire time so the 'Loading latest-snapshot indexes...' status message never renders.

Fix options (pick one or combine):

1. Background-thread the load on app startup. Show a spinner/progress in the Find & Restore page until loaded. First user query is then instant.

2. Stream the wbadmin index and match in-place against the query instead of materializing all hits into memory. Slower per-query but no startup cost.

3. Pre-filter the wbadmin index to user-relevant paths only (Users/, dev/) and skip Windows/Program Files/ system paths. Loses fidelity for restoring system files but covers the common case.

title: Investigate Bitdefender HTTPS interception breaking IPv6 to management.azure.com
description: Discovered 2026-04-27 while creating Trusted Signing profile. curl/az/PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod all fail with TLS connection reset over IPv6 to management.azure.com (resolves to arm-msedge.net 2603:1030:a0b::10) but work fine over IPv4 (4.150.240.10). Other Microsoft endpoints like graph.microsoft.com and login.microsoftonline.com work over IPv6. Disabling Bitdefender + firewall did NOT fix it; ruling out Bitdefender SSL inspection but suggests something else (Comcast IPv6 routing? Windows TLS profile? Anycast-to-Anycast asymmetry?). Workaround in place: 'curl -4' for ARM REST calls. Memory entry: network-management-azure-com-is-reachable-only-over.
notes:
2026-05-07: Diagnosed and fixed.

Original hypothesis (Bitdefender HTTPS interception, Comcast IPv6 routing) was wrong. Real cause: HTTP/2 ALPN handshake to management.azure.com over IPv6 is reset at the TLS layer. Reproduction:
- curl -6 with libcurl-without-HTTP/2 → works (negotiates HTTP/1.1)
- curl -6 --http1.1 → works
- Invoke-WebRequest -HttpVersion 1.1 → works
- Invoke-WebRequest (default, attempts HTTP/2) → "SSL connection forcibly closed" during handshake
- az rest (urllib3 attempts HTTP/2) → ConnectionResetError 10054
- Test-NetConnection -Port 443 → succeeds (TCP layer fine)
- IPv4: all of the above work with HTTP/2

The 4/27 reproduction looked like total IPv6 failure because the bundled curl on this host was built without nghttp2 and silently downgraded to HTTP/1.1 — so it appeared to work in some tests but not others, depending on which client library was used.

Fix applied: pinned management.azure.com -> 4.150.240.10 (Azure Front Door IPv4 anycast) in C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts (line 51, dated marker). Result: Dns.GetHostAddresses returns IPv4 only, IWR returns HTTP 400 normally, az rest returns subscription JSON. No more `-4` workaround needed.

Caveat: ARM frontdoor IPv4 anycast IP could rotate over time. If az/Invoke-RestMethod ever start failing again with NXDOMAIN or wrong-cert errors, re-resolve with `Resolve-DnsName management.azure.com -Type A -DnsOnly` and update the hosts entry.

Closing — investigation done, workaround productized.
